_source: RF-GUI-01..05, RNF-USA-05 with ADR-017 (max 4 steps). Reference clinical protocols: require validation by Flight Surgeon personnel.

inventory.kit_alpha: Med Kit Alpha (diagnostics: BP cuff, pulse oximeter, Amsler grid, urinalysis strips)
inventory.kit_bravo: Med Kit Bravo (medications: antiemetic, analgesic, oral radioprotective cocktail)
inventory.compression: Elastic venous compression cuffs (Med Kit Alpha)

CM-ENV-01.title: CO₂ leak or poor ventilation
CM-ENV-01.what: Cabin air is accumulating carbon dioxide (CO₂) and your blood oxygen is dropping. Brain and muscles receive less oxygen.

steps.text: Alert the crew and move to the best-ventilated module.
Turn on forced-circulation fans and switch CDRA to forced cycle.
Install a fresh LiOH canister in the emergency holder.
Measure SpO₂ with the pulse oximeter every 10 min until ppCO₂ drops below 2.0.

CM-ENV-01.fsMessage: R-ENV-01: ppCO₂ and SpO₂ with timestamps, filters replaced, SpO₂ after 30 min.

CM-ENV-02.title: CO₂-induced headache
CM-ENV-02.what: A CO₂ pocket formed in the cabin: without gravity, air does not mix on its own. Elevated CO₂ dilates cerebral vessels and causes headache. The cause is environmental, not illness.

steps.text: Check forced-circulation fans and replace the CDRA sorbent bed.
Move to the best-ventilated module and rest.
Install an LiOH canister if ppCO₂ remains above 3.0.
Take 1 analgesic from Med Kit Bravo only if headache persists after 30 min.

CM-ENV-02.fsMessage: R-ENV-02: ppCO₂, headache severity (1-10), Amsler result, and medication taken.

CM-SANS-01.title: Acute SANS: vision and pressure
CM-SANS-01.what: In microgravity, fluids shift to the head and press on the eye (SANS: spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome). High blood pressure worsens it.

steps.text: Don the LBNP suit and depressurize to −35 mmHg for 60 min.
Perform the Amsler grid test on this screen at 0 min and 60 min.
Limit dietary sodium intake to less than 2.0 g per day.

CM-SANS-01.fsMessage: R-SANS-01: SBP pre/post LBNP, Amsler at 0 and 60 min per eye, sodium intake, and onset date of blurred vision.

CM-SANS-02.title: High blood pressure with short sleep
CM-SANS-02.what: Short sleep combined with elevated blood pressure increases fluid pressure in the head. It is a precursor to SANS.

steps.text: Schedule 8 h of sleep tonight with cabin lighting set to red mode.
Complete an LBNP session at −30 mmHg for 45 min.
Measure blood pressure tomorrow upon waking.

CM-RAD-01.title: Solar storm: move to shelter
CM-RAD-01.what: A solar storm launches high-energy particles that penetrate the hull and damage cells. The storm shelter provides higher shielding.

steps.text: Evacuate to the central module storm shelter in under 5 min.
Take the oral radioprotective cocktail from Med Kit Bravo.
Place personal passive dosimeters on the interior bulkhead.
Exit only after dose rate drops below 35 µSv/h for 1 hour.

CM-RAD-01.fsMessage: R-RAD-01: shelter entry time, peak dose rate (µSv/h), cumulative dose, and symptoms.

CM-RAD-02.title: Solar storm with nausea
CM-RAD-02.what: Nausea during a solar particle storm can be the earliest warning sign of high radiation exposure.

steps.text: Enter the storm shelter and secure the hatch immediately.
Take 1 antiemetic from Med Kit Bravo with a small sip of water.
Log the time of first emesis or severe nausea on this screen.
Drink 250 ml of water every hour while inside the shelter.

CM-RAD-02.fsMessage: R-RAD-02: nausea onset time, emesis count, peak dose rate, antiemetic, and time.

CM-COG-01.title: Fatigue and disrupted sleep rhythm
CM-COG-01.what: Short sleep with low heart rate variability indicates poor autonomic recovery. Error rate and reaction time worsen.

steps.text: Avoid safety-critical tasks (EVA, maneuvering) for the next 24 h.
Turn off screens 1 h before sleep and enable red lighting mode.
Sleep 8 h in crew quarters with sleep mask.

CM-REN-01.title: Suspected renal calculus
CM-REN-01.what: Bones lose calcium in microgravity. Excess calcium enters urine and can form a kidney stone, causing lumbar pain.

steps.text: Drink 500 ml of water now and 250 ml every hour.
Take 1 analgesic from Med Kit Bravo if pain exceeds 5 out of 10.
Run a urinalysis dipstick from Med Kit Alpha and log any hematuria.
Notify CMO if fever appears or pain rises to 8 out of 10.

CM-REN-01.fsMessage: R-REN-01: urinary calcium, pain scale (1-10), dipstick result, and medication taken.

CM-REN-02.title: Elevated urinary calcium
CM-REN-02.what: Bones are shedding calcium due to unloading in microgravity. Higher hydration and resistive loading slow bone loss.

steps.text: Drink at least 2.5 L of water today.
Perform 60 min of ARED with full lower-body load.
Repeat urinary calcium measurement in 3 days.

CM-CARD-01.title: Orthostatic dizziness
CM-CARD-01.what: Without gravity, the heart adapts to pumping less effortfully. On standing, blood pools in the legs and brain perfusion drops.

steps.text: Sit down or brace immediately and wait 2 min.
Drink 500 ml of water with a salted broth ration.
Complete an LBNP session at −30 mmHg for 30 min.
Measure standing pulse and blood pressure upon completion.

CM-IND-hr.title: Heart rate out of range
CM-IND-hr.what: Your resting heart rate is faster or slower than expected.

steps.text: Rest seated quietly for 10 min without speaking.
Re-measure pulse using the pulse oximeter.
Drink 300 ml of water.
Notify CMO if heart rate remains out of range.

CM-IND-hr.fsMessage: Resting HR (3 readings), prior activity, and symptoms.

CM-IND-hrv.title: Low heart rate variability
CM-IND-hrv.what: Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects nervous system recovery. Low values indicate accumulated stress or fatigue.

steps.text: Perform 5 min of slow paced breathing: 6 breaths per minute.
Swap today’s intense workout for 30 min light cycle ergometer.
Get 8 h of sleep tonight.

CM-IND-hrv.fsMessage: Last 3 days of HRV, sleep hours, and workload.

CM-IND-sbp.title: High systolic blood pressure
CM-IND-sbp.what: Arterial pressure during heart contraction is elevated. In microgravity, this drives extra fluid toward the head and eyes.

steps.text: Measure seated blood pressure after 5 min of quiet rest.
Cut sodium today: select meals labeled low-sodium.
Complete an LBNP session at −30 mmHg for 45 min.

CM-IND-sbp.fsMessage: SBP/DBP (3 readings), visual symptoms, and LBNP sessions.

CM-IND-dbp.title: High diastolic blood pressure
CM-IND-dbp.what: Resting vascular pressure between heartbeats is elevated. It commonly rises with short sleep and stress.

steps.text: Measure seated blood pressure after 5 min of quiet rest.
Get 8 h of sleep tonight.
Perform 30 min of light cycle ergometer exercise.

CM-IND-spo2.title: Low blood oxygen saturation
CM-IND-spo2.what: Blood is carrying less oxygen than normal. Cause may be cabin atmosphere or ventilation.

steps.text: Check cabin ppCO₂ and O₂ on the Habitat view.
If SpO₂ is below 93, move to the best-ventilated module and notify CMO.
Re-check SpO₂ on another finger with the pulse oximeter.

CM-IND-spo2.fsMessage: SpO₂ (3 readings), cabin ppCO₂ and O₂ at the same time.

CM-IND-glucose.title: Fasting glucose out of range
CM-IND-glucose.what: Fasting blood sugar is higher or lower than the expected range.

steps.text: Repeat measurement with a fresh test strip from Med Kit Alpha.
If low (below 75), take a juice pouch or glucose gel.
If high (above 105), drink 300 ml water and walk 20 min on treadmill.

CM-IND-glucose.fsMessage: Blood glucose (2 readings), time of last meal.

CM-IND-temp.title: Elevated body temperature
CM-IND-temp.what: Body temperature is above normal. It can reflect infection or heat retention after exercise.

steps.text: Rest 30 min without exercise and re-measure temperature.
Drink 500 ml of water.
Take 1 antipyretic from Med Kit Bravo if above 38.0 °C.

CM-IND-temp.fsMessage: Temperature curve, associated symptoms, and medication taken.

CM-IND-sleep.title: Short sleep duration
CM-IND-sleep.what: Insufficient sleep impairs alertness and physiological recovery.

steps.text: Switch displays to red mode starting 2 h before bedtime.
Avoid intense exercise within 3 h of sleep.
Schedule 8 h of sleep using sleep mask and earplugs.

CM-IND-sleep.fsMessage: Sleep hours over the last 3 days and duty shifts.

CM-IND-mood.title: Low mood score
CM-IND-mood.what: Isolation and routine can lower mood. This is common in long missions and manageable.

steps.text: Spend 10 min talking with a crewmate about how you feel.
Perform 30 min on treadmill or cycle ergometer.
Book a private personal message during the next comm window.

CM-IND-mood.fsMessage: Last 5 days of mood scores and notable stressors.

CM-IND-urineCa.title: Bone calcium loss
CM-IND-urineCa.what: Urinary calcium rises when bones demineralize due to mechanical unloading.

steps.text: Perform 60 min of ARED with full leg and hip load.
Drink at least 2.5 L of water today.
Repeat urinary calcium measurement in 3 days.

CM-IND-urineCa.fsMessage: Urinary calcium series, weekly ARED minutes.

CM-IND-ppco2.title: Elevated cabin CO₂
CM-IND-ppco2.what: Cabin air contains more CO₂ than recommended. Can trigger headache and fatigue.

steps.text: Verify CDRA is powered and fault-free.
Clear any obstructions from module ventilation grilles.
Install an LiOH canister if ppCO₂ exceeds 3.0.

CM-IND-ppco2.fsMessage: ppCO₂ series, CDRA status, and LiOH canisters used.

CM-IND-pressure.title: Cabin pressure out of range
CM-IND-pressure.what: Spacecraft air pressure deviates from nominal. A drop may indicate a hull leak.

steps.text: Notify Commander and all crew members.
Close inter-module hatches per depressurization procedure.
Read pressure in each module every 5 min on this screen.

CM-IND-pressure.fsMessage: Module pressure series, hatches closed, and timestamps.

CM-IND-o2.title: Cabin oxygen out of range
CM-IND-o2.what: Cabin oxygen fraction is outside nominal limits. Too low causes fatigue; too high increases fire hazard.

steps.text: Notify the Commander.
If O₂ is high, power down spark-producing equipment.
If O₂ is low, check your SpO₂ with the pulse oximeter.

CM-IND-o2.fsMessage: Cabin O₂ series and corrective actions taken.

CM-IND-radiation.title: Elevated background radiation
CM-IND-radiation.what: Dose rate is rising. Not yet a full solar storm, but exposure should be minimized.

steps.text: Defer non-urgent tasks in lightly shielded modules.
Keep access path to the storm shelter unobstructed.
Monitor dose rate continuously on the Habitat tab.

CM-IND-radiation.fsMessage: Dose rate series and cumulative mission dose.

CM-DRIFT-01.title: Drifting toward caution threshold
CM-DRIFT-01.what: Current value is still nominal, but the 7-day trend projects it will exit nominal range soon.

steps.text: Review the 7-day trend chart for this indicator.
Apply today’s daily countermeasure (exercise, hydration, or sleep).
Log tomorrow’s measurement at the same time of day.

CM-DRIFT-02.title: Unusual value vs. baseline
CM-DRIFT-02.what: Reading deviates significantly from your days 1-14 personal baseline even if within population bounds.

steps.text: Repeat the measurement to rule out sensor artifact.
Note any unusual sleep, meal, or exercise change yesterday.
Log tomorrow’s measurement at the same time of day.

CM-DRIFT-03.title: Less sleep with rising diastolic pressure
CM-DRIFT-03.what: This week you are sleeping less while resting vascular pressure rises. Together they precede cardiovascular and visual strain.

steps.text: Schedule 8 h of sleep for the next 3 nights.
Enable red display mode starting 2 h before bedtime.
Do 30 min of light cycle ergometer in the morning.
Measure blood pressure tomorrow upon waking.

CM-IND-cabinTemp.title: Cabin temperature out of range
CM-IND-cabinTemp.what: Module air is too cold or too warm. Affects sleep, cognitive performance, and hydration.

steps.text: Notify Commander to inspect module thermal control.
If cabin is hot, drink 300 ml of water every hour.
Defer strenuous exercise until temperature returns to nominal.

CM-IND-cabinTemp.fsMessage: Cabin temperature series and corrective actions taken.

CM-IND-humidity.title: Cabin humidity out of range
CM-IND-humidity.what: Air is too dry or too humid. Dry air irritates eyes and throat; high humidity promotes condensation and mold.

steps.text: Notify Commander to inspect humidity control.
If air is dry, drink an extra 300 ml of water.
Inspect cold module surfaces for condensation.

CM-IND-humidity.fsMessage: Relative humidity series and corrective actions taken.

CM-SANS-01-ALT.title: SANS without LBNP: fallback
CM-SANS-01-ALT.what: LBNP is inoperable. Without gravity, fluids pool in the head and press on the eye (SANS). Torso elevation and leg compression help shift fluid downward.

steps.text: Elevate torso 30° relative to the head axis and hold that posture.
Apply elastic venous compression cuffs on both thighs.
Perform the Amsler grid test on this screen at 0 min and 60 min.
Limit dietary sodium intake to less than 2.0 g per day.

CM-SANS-01-ALT.fsMessage: R-SANS-01 with LBNP inoperable: SBP pre/post, Amsler at 0 and 60 min, torso elevation duration, and compression.

glossary.CO₂: carbon dioxide, the gas exhaled during respiration
glossary.SpO₂: blood oxygen saturation, measured with the pulse oximeter
glossary.LBNP: lower body negative pressure suit that shifts fluids back toward the legs
glossary.CDRA: carbon dioxide removal assembly that scrubs CO₂ from cabin air
glossary.LiOH: lithium hydroxide canister that absorbs CO₂ in emergencies
glossary.SANS: spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome: cephalic fluid pressure on the eye
glossary.ARED: advanced resistive exercise device that loads bones and muscles
glossary.SBP: systolic blood pressure, the upper pressure reading
glossary.DBP: diastolic blood pressure, the lower pressure reading
glossary.HRV: heart rate variability: beat-to-beat timing variation
glossary.EVA: extravehicular activity, spacewalk outside the spacecraft
glossary.CANS: compact neutron dosimeter aboard the spacecraft
